doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Higgins, Hendrix and the spiritual path
title: Tenderness versus power in saxophone playing
summary: Lloyd says Prez moves him with tenderness, that Cannonball's band demanded strong playing, and quotes Robin Williams on not hurting the saxophone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: But we used to play together a lot in New York. See here's the thing... There was a time when a transition was happening, but I always heard melodies that were in the air that were given to me.

I never tried misuse my instrument. This guy said... Robin Williams told me once, he said he got a saxophone and he was trying to play and he sound so horrible. He said... he was at a session and some black guy came over to him and said "Don't hurt it."
"Don't hurt it." You know [laughs] because, but my point is that, prayers move me with tenderness.
I don't have a problem with that, but something about tenderness. So when I went with Cannon and them I had to play real strong.
So you have to, what did Blakey say? "Make sure the punishment fits the crime."
